claim: AAAI 2026 accepted EAGLE, a calibration method that reads confidence from intermediate hidden layers during self-evaluation rather than from the model's final output token, arguing intermediate layers carry more faithful uncertainty signal.
stance_target: reading confidence purely from a final-layer/output-token signal (as DPRC's tokenized-digit readout does)
scope_conditions: LLM self-evaluation-based confidence calibration, especially RLHF'd models
quoted_support: Instead of relying on the model's final output, our approach extracts internal beliefs from multiple intermediate layers during self-evaluation.

claim: RLHF'd LLMs exhibit overconfidence and generate plausible-but-incorrect answers, motivating internal-state-based calibration methods.
stance_target: why calibration matters for RLHF'd models
quoted_support: This overconfidence, especially in models undergone Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), poses significant challenges for reliable uncertainty estimation and safe deployment.

claim: EAGLE's accepted AAAI 2026 paper includes in-depth mechanistic analyses (layer-wise uncertainty patterns, self-evaluation prompt sensitivity, score-range effects) beyond the headline method, indicating AAAI rewards mechanism-level ablation depth alongside a new method.
stance_target: expected ablation depth for an accepted AAAI calibration method paper
quoted_support: We also provide an in-depth analysis of EAGLE, including a layer-wise examination of uncertainty patterns, a study of the impact of self-evaluation prompts, and an analysis of the effect of self-evaluation score range.
